module_title: Advent of Europeans in India - Basic Understanding
introduction: In the 15th century, the search for a direct sea route for the lucrative spice trade (especially black pepper) brought European companies to India. The Portuguese were the first to arrive, followed by other European powers. At this level, we will understand their sequence of arrival and basic early details.

core_concepts.title: Arrival of the Portuguese
core_concepts.description: Vasco da Gama reached the port of Calicut in India via the Cape of Good Hope (Africa) in 1498. He was welcomed by the local Hindu ruler, 'Zamorin'.

core_concepts.title: Sequence of Arrival
core_concepts.description: The correct sequence of European powers arriving in India for trade is: Portuguese -> Dutch -> English -> Danish -> French.

core_concepts.title: Establishment of the East India Company (EIC)
core_concepts.description: On December 31, 1600, Queen Elizabeth I of Britain granted a royal charter to the 'East India Company', giving them a monopoly to trade with the East.

core_concepts.title: Early Factories
core_concepts.description: These companies established trade centers known as 'factories'. The Portuguese set up their first factory in Cochin (1503), and the English established their first permanent factory in Surat (1613).

important_entities.name: Vasco da Gama
important_entities.significance: The first European sailor to reach India directly by sea in 1498, bypassing the traditional land routes controlled by Arab and Ottoman traders.

important_entities.name: Captain William Hawkins
important_entities.significance: He arrived in Surat on the ship 'Hector' in 1608 and visited Mughal Emperor Jahangir's court in Agra to seek trade concessions.

important_entities.name: Zamorin
important_entities.significance: He welcomed Vasco da Gama, but relations with the Portuguese later soured due to pressure from Arab merchants.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often get confused. The sequence of 'establishment' of companies is Portuguese (1498) -> English (1600) -> Dutch (1602). However, the sequence of 'arrival' in India is Portuguese (1498) -> Dutch (1605) -> English (1608).
During that time, a 'factory' was not a manufacturing unit. It was simply a fortified warehouse for goods and a residential complex for the merchants (called 'factors').

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: P- Portuguese, D- Dutch, E- English, D- Danish, F- French. Remembering this acronym helps answer chronological sequence questions.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the year Vasco da Gama arrived (1498) and the port (Calicut).
Questions about the location of the first English factory (Surat) and the envoy who visited Jahangir's court (Captain Hawkins) are frequently asked.
